subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw define and own a public memory-dreaming plugin protocol and scheduler contract, or keep dreaming orchestration plugin-owned/ClawHub-only until the memory role-slot direction lands?
rationale: Current main only provides slot-owned config lookup plus a memory-core sidecar engine; adding the requested lifecycle protocol would create durable public plugin SDK, config, scheduler, and state semantics that automation should not choose.

options.title: Coordinate With Role-Slot PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as related architecture context before deciding the specific dreaming lifecycle contract.

options.title: Sponsor A Dreaming Protocol
options.body: Define a documented SDK/provider contract with memory-core compatibility, docs, contract tests, and proof from at least one non-core memory plugin.

options.title: Keep Dreaming Plugin-Owned
options.body: Document ClawHub/plugin-owned dreaming as the supported path and close this only if maintainers explicitly reject OpenClaw-managed generic dreaming orchestration.

recommendation.title: Coordinate With Role-Slot PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as related architecture context before deciding the specific dreaming lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is public product/API direction, and CONTRIBUTING.md lists Peter Steinberger as the project decision owner.
